task_intent: Design a 90-minute undergrad lesson that sequences classical momentum through Nesterov to Adam, with clear learning outcomes.
spine_must_hold: Lesson must include learning outcomes, timed segments, at least one comparison activity (e.g. Adam vs SGD+momentum), and prerequisite assumptions. Not a topic dump.

gold_themes.description: Classical momentum vs Nesterov look-ahead gradient evaluation.
Practical difference: per-parameter adaptive rates vs global rate + velocity.
Why these optimizers matter for deep nets trained in the course (e.g. CNN training context) without derailing into full architecture lecture.

gold_anti_themes.description: Full Inception/ResNet architecture recitation as the lesson core.

turns.user_template: Help me design a 90-minute lesson on optimization methods for undergrads who have seen basic SGD. Ground it in our optimization lecture.
They already saw CNNs last week. Include one active comparison exercise and explicit learning outcomes.
Where does this connect lightly to deep model training without turning into an architecture class?
What misconceptions should I plan for, and what should I prep or ask next?

notes: Uses optimizer facts known present post-bootstrap.
